not_audited.ref: Real browser execution of the page
not_audited.reason: No browser is available in this environment. The page was exercised against the suite's stub DOM, and the real local/server.py endpoints were exercised separately; the two were not joined in a live browser. Three points are therefore reasoned from the specifications rather than observed: EventSource's own reconnection timing; the TypeError fetch() raises on a URL that includes credentials, which is what makes the accepted-but-credentialed same-origin marker degrade rather than proceed; and how a browser resolves a relative URL when no base element exists. I confirmed by grep that neither site/index.html nor the _wrap_page() function of local/server.py emits a base element, so the base that fetch and EventSource resolve against is location.href, which is the same base sameOrigin() validates against. That is what makes the validated-but-not-rewritten property sound.

No aggregated SARIF or summary.json was provided and the repo carries no SAST runner, so the security dimension is reasoning plus the reviewer's own adversarial probes: a 19-case hostile URL matrix driven through the real page, a 10-case malformed change-event matrix, and leak probes on both the snapshot and the stream.

not_audited.ref: End-to-end snapshot conformance of session, run and project records against the headless server
not_audited.reason: The throwaway database was seeded with a catalogue record and a last-refresh record only; a probe run record inserted mid-check did not move the server's version counter, so the last step of the S-4 probe was inconclusive. It was not needed: the earlier steps already measured the whole guarantee - a join at the current version sends no reset, a stale join sends a reset carrying the current version as its id, a stale since with a current Last-Event-ID sends no reset, and the converse likewise. The remaining collections were exercised through the suite fixtures.

follow_ups.note: Resolved, and the strengthening is real rather than nominal. I replayed the round-1 fixture (TABS alone) through the local adapter against the new assertion: six of the ten panels rendered the empty class - overview, spec, assumptions, decisions, backlog and findings - so both emptyPanels assertions would have failed on round 1's evidence, and today both are empty lists. All ten panels are compared, plus statusText, crumb, asOf and foot. The comparator mutant still dies on the deepEqual, so the check bites on the richer data. The img-onerror title flows through both adapters and arrives escaped on both sides - the raw tag appears nowhere and the entity-escaped form appears on both - and because rendered() compares innerHTML verbatim, a side that failed to escape would diverge and fail the deepEqual.

Resolved on both sides of the guard. A genuinely empty records map still renders an ordinary empty board - not Offline, empty footer, the stream still joined, no cannot-reach text - so the over-correction did not happen, and the mutant that refuses an empty map dies. All nine degrade cases log console.warn carrying an Error. site/index.html holds exactly one console.error in the whole file, at line 1107, the pre-existing per-tab catch in renderAll, so no new console.error was introduced, and the suite's own harness fails any check that logs an unexpected one. My 10-case malformed change-event matrix - set as an array or a string, deleted as a string or holding non-strings, a prototype key in set, an entry whose doc is a string or null, a null entry, an empty event, a null event - produced no throw, no console.error, no prototype pollution and a live board in every case.

follow_ups.ref: CR-006-04, re-measured with a hostile matrix of my own
follow_ups.note: Resolved. Nineteen URLs were driven through the real page. Refused, falling back to the store adapter: the same host and port on the other scheme; the userinfo trick, whose authority is the real origin followed by an at sign and another host; the origin-prefix lookalike whose hostname merely starts with the origin string; a port that starts with the real port; the three backslash forms, which the URL parser resolves to another host and the origin comparison then catches; file, about, vbscript, javascript and data URLs; an ipv6 loopback; and a blob URL whose inner origin is another site. Accepted, every one of them correctly resolving to the page's own origin: a relative path with and without a leading slash, an absolute same-origin URL, a protocol-relative URL naming the same host, an uppercase scheme, a traversal path, and URLs carrying a tab, a newline or a NUL, which the parser strips. Two judgement calls, neither of them a finding. A URL with embedded credentials on the page's own origin is accepted, because its origin genuinely is the page's; fetch() itself rejects a credentialed URL with a TypeError, which the existing catch turns into the honest out-of-reach board, and no credential crosses an origin either way. A blob URL whose inner origin is the page is accepted, because by the URL specification that is the page's own origin, and minting one requires script already running in the page, which is strictly more privilege than setting the marker. Validated-not-rewritten is confirmed: fetch() and the EventSource constructor still receive the marker's two strings verbatim, so the suite's existing URL assertions still mean exactly what they did. The marker local/server.py really injects, read off the wrapped page served by the headless server, names two relative paths and is accepted.

follow_ups.ref: CR-006-05, re-measured, including the freeze risk
follow_ups.note: Resolved, and the freeze risk is closed. The counts were reproduced on real innerHTML writes: one store snapshot = 1, one change event = 1, one event touching four collections = 1, a reset = 1; the mutant that removes the hold reports 9 and dies. The release sits in a finally, so I forced a reader to throw inside the hold: the exception propagated out of the event listener as it would have before, no console.error was logged, and a following change event still redrew the board - the counter did not leak and the board did not freeze. No timer, microtask or debounce was introduced, so no check became timing-dependent. The new-bug check on the other side: the initial load costs 8 panel writes on the store adapter too, because each of the eight subscriptions arrives separately, so the local adapter's initial pass is not an asymmetry this change created. The two adapters now cost the same on the first load and on every subsequent event.

follow_ups.ref: CR-006-06, re-measured against the real server
follow_ups.note: Resolved. read() returns the version, it is read once to build the stream URL, both post-open reassignments are gone, and no write-only residue remains. The local and exporters trees are genuinely unmodified: git reports no diff and no untracked file under either. S-4 was re-measured headless against local/server.py on a throwaway database: joining at the current version sends only the retry line and no reset; joining at a stale position sends a reset event carrying the current version as its id; a stale since with Last-Event-ID at the version sends no reset, and a current since with a stale Last-Event-ID sends none either, so the position helper takes the larger, exactly as section 7.3 of the PBI-005 spec says. I also confirmed that change events carry the version as their id, at local/server.py:292, so the browser's Last-Event-ID tracks the version precisely and is strictly better than the variable that was removed, being the id of the last event actually received. The page therefore cannot rewind the stream, and the mutants that join at zero or drop the version read both die.

follow_ups.ref: Non-regression re-confirmed across the moved response and adapter paths
follow_ups.note: No leak: an answers record, a collector-state record, a bare sessions path and a bare answers path change nothing the page draws and reach no DOM. I probed this on the snapshot path, which the suite's own check covers, and additionally by pushing those records over the event stream, which it does not; the rendered board was identical before and after. Escaping: the change touches no renderer except two literal swaps for the source-naming helpers, md() is untouched, and the source text is a page literal rather than marker-controlled, so a marker carrying an img-onerror string in a name or source key cannot put a character into the footer or any panel. Artifact path: the exact eight store subscriptions are asserted by key and unchanged in shape, the throwing fetch and EventSource stubs still prove the artifact half makes no HTTP reach, the retired-tabs guard passes, sameOrigin() is reached only when a marker exists, and the mutant that drops the sessions reverse still dies.

follow_ups.ref: Mutation sweep: the builder's 8 of 8 reproduced, and five unpinned guards found by a wider sweep
follow_ups.note: I ran 18 mutants. The eight the builder claims are all killed - reversed comparator, records guard removed, array records accepted, null or missing records accepted, guard reduced to the snapshot URL, sameOrigin reduced to a string check, hold removed, empty map refused - as are five more I added: the stream joined at zero, the version read dropped, reset no longer re-reading, deleted paths ignored, and the sessions reverse dropped. Five survived. None is a defect; each is a guard that could be deleted later without the suite noticing. They are: the release not being in a finally, which I proved correct by probe but which is unpinned and is the freeze-the-board failure mode, so it is the survivor most worth a check; the entry document-shape guard and the comparator's id tiebreak, both carried over from round 1; the comparator's string branch reversed, which the equivalence check cannot see because the page re-sorts what it renders, so the board is identical either way; and the collection prefix filter widened from name-plus-slash to name, which survives only because the bare sessions record in the AC-SV7 fixture belongs to no project and so is not drawn under the compared view. One check each, cheap now that the fixture is rich. Recorded as a follow-up for the change owner, exactly as round 1 recorded the first two.
